title: reconcile status-flow errors hardcode backlog/config.yml regardless of the active tracker backend
summary: On a quest-backed workspace, lore check's status-flow errors send the reader to backlog/config.yml — a file that does not exist and would not be read. The flow itself comes from adapter.statusFlow(), which is backend-polymorphic; only the message is hardcoded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The three status-flow errors in src/core/reconcile.ts (lines 155, 165, 237) name the ACTIVE backend's status-flow source, not backlog/config.yml unconditionally
On a quest-backed workspace the hint points at the quest status flow (quest task status-flow) and/or the [reconcile.overrides] escape hatch, and never at a nonexistent file
A regression test covers the quest-backend wording, so the Backlog-only phrasing cannot silently come back
The Backlog-backed wording is unchanged for a Backlog workspace

finalSummary:
Delivered in PR #105, green on CI run 34983645053 (10 pass, 2 skipped, 0 fail) against head 2a659743.

WHAT WAS WRONG: the three status-flow throws in src/core/reconcile.ts named `backlog/config.yml` as a literal while the flow itself came from the backend-polymorphic adapter.statusFlow(). On this repo — quest-backed since the 2026-09-03 cutover — every one of them sent the reader to a file that does not exist and would not be read.

THE FIX FOLLOWS A PRECEDENT THIS REPO ALREADY SET rather than inventing one. LCLI-494 fixed the identical defect shape on the projection side, where every record claimed 'backlog-json/1' regardless of the backend that produced it, by putting sourceAdapterVersion on the TrackerAdapter interface. Its own doc comment records why the interface, not a literal: a new backend cannot be added without supplying one. statusFlowHints sits next to it for the same reason.

WHY COMPLETE HINTS AND NOT AN INTERPOLATED FILENAME: the advice genuinely differs by backend, not just the path. A Backlog project fixes a degenerate flow by editing `statuses:`; a Quest workspace has no such key to edit at all (its flow comes from the workspace lifecycle policy, read back with `quest task status-flow`); Jira's flow is lore's own `[tracker.jira] status_flow` in .lore/config.toml, neither a Backlog file nor anything Jira serves. That third distinct answer is the reason a backlog-or-quest boolean would have been wrong — worth recording, because the boolean is the obvious first design. The one shared element, the `[reconcile.overrides]` escape hatch, lives in .lore/config.toml for every backend and is appended once rather than repeated three times where it could drift.

AC#4 (Backlog wording unchanged) IS SATISFIED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by care: the new parameter defaults to Backlog's constant, whose strings are the previous literals byte for byte, and a test asserts that omitting the argument and passing BACKLOG_STATUS_FLOW_HINTS explicitly produce the same hint. A caller written before this change cannot silently drift.

EVIDENCE BEYOND THE TESTS. `bun run src/cli.ts check` against this real quest-backed repo now prints: 'the task's status must match one of the statuses `quest task status-flow` reports, exactly, or add a `[reconcile.overrides]` entry for it in .lore/config.toml'. Previously that line named backlog/config.yml. It still exits 6 — that is LCLI-504's pre-existing red (LCLI-333 carries the off-flow status 'Blocked'), untouched here and correctly so.

ALL THREE SITES WERE MUTATION-TESTED, each reverted to its old literal in turn. The classify() mutation failed 2 tests; the validateStatusFlow() mutation failed 2 DIFFERENT tests. A new test that passes first time may be asserting the wrong thing; these were checked by breaking the fix.

Full suite 3058 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail. typecheck exit 0. lint exit 0 (one warning, confirmed pre-existing by stashing rather than assumed).

FILED SEPARATELY, NOT FOLDED IN: LCLI-506 — ADR-0009 still specifies the status vocabulary as read from Backlog config (lines 50, 138, 205) and no ADR supersedes it. That is the same staleness one layer up, in the architecture of record. Amending versus superseding an ADR is a decision about the record, and the fleet's retirement-scope rule says history is left alone rather than rewritten, so it is not a thing to do quietly inside a code fix.

ALSO WORTH CARRYING TO LCLI-504: classify() already threads a pausedStatus, and its comment cites 'Quest 0.4.0's Blocked' (LCLI-455). `quest task status-flow` now reports pausedStatus: Paused. LCLI-333's 'Blocked' is therefore a STALE LABEL from before quest renamed it, not an arbitrary off-flow value — which points at 'Paused' as the honest resolution for AC#2 there, and raises the question of whether other repos' records carry the same stale label.
